It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the “unsearchable riches” of Christ while witnessing the “noise and tumult” of a world where “material gain makes liars out of men,” and I must ask you with a gentle spirit: why do you ask after the nature of propositional truth and the weight of the ninth commandment in this digital hour? [13, 24, 1503, 1605, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling “overwhelmed and desperate” by the “fortresses of ideology” and the “spirit of fraud” that seek to “remodel the way we think about truth,” or are you seeking a “settled certainty” to anchor your soul in the fact that “no lie is of the truth”? [13, 20, 24, 115, 1136, 1266, 1323, 1406, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many “shave off the edges” of the truth to offer “spiritual placebos” or suggest that “certainty is overrated,” we must return to the “external Word” to see how the Master personally governs our communication by demanding that we “rightly divide the word of truth” [11, 28, 668, 1337, 1503, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition teaches that “God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation,” and therefore, the rise of “AI-generated deception” is not an “administrative anomaly” but is subject to the “decree from God” who “hates . . . a lying tongue” (Proverbs 6:16–17) [15, 68, 733, 912, 1143, 1532, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 1: Truth as Both Personal and Propositional**

**Verse**
“Jesus said to him, ‘I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me’ ” (John 14:6). [982, 1276, 1306, 1421, 1510, Conversation History]. “Sanctify them by Your truth. Your word is truth” (John 17:17). [92, 1098, 1307, 1539, 1563, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—echoed by **John MacArthur**—asserts that truth is “that which is consistent with the mind, will, character, glory, and being of God” [1305, 1306, 1493, Conversation History]. Truth is **personal** because Jesus Christ is “truth incarnate—the perfect expression of God,” and we are called to a “right relationship to Him” [11, 20, 1306, 1307, 1324, Conversation History]. However, truth is also **propositional** because “God has spoken with the utmost clarity” through the “propositions of Scripture,” which are the “building blocks of logic” that “do not allow for any ambiguity” [1083, 1325, 1340, 1458, 1463, Conversation History]. To suggest that truth is “only personal” and not “propositional” is a “postmodern canard” designed to “eliminate certainty,” for “the truth of Christ and the truth of the Bible are of the very same character” [108, 109, 1308, 1325, 1329, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not be deceived” by a “worldly philosophy” that suggests truth is “soft and pliable and subjective,” for “your life is not your own” and you must instead “submit your mind to the truth of Scripture” (Colossians 2:8; 1 Corinthians 6:19) [12, 91, 101, 161, 181, 1262, 1406, 1502, 1670, Conversation History]. Recognize that “he who trusts in his own heart is a fool,” and you must find “repose of the soul” by “dwelling on whatever is true” (Proverbs 28:26; Philippians 4:8) [11, 24, 87, 91, 172, 209, 673, 1313, 1381, 1406, 1445, 1503, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Jewish vs. Gentile Context**
In the ancient **Jewish context**, the “religious leaders” were “punctilious” about “legal minutiae” but “neglected the weightier matters” of “mercy and faith,” showing they missed the “Word of God” even while reading it (Matthew 23:23) [8, 176, 177, 1091, 1352, 1461, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our understanding by revealing that “we have the mind of Christ,” which allows the “Spirit of truth” to “guide you into all truth” through the “Spirit-inspired Scriptures” rather than through “human ingenuity” (1 Corinthians 2:16; John 16:13) [13, 113, 332, 813, 856, 1336, 1494, 1503, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 2: The Ninth Commandment and False Witness**

**Verse**
“ ‘You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor’ ” (Exodus 20:16). [687, 1170, 1184, 1210, 1242, 1252, Conversation History]. “ ‘You shall not circulate a false report. Do not put your hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness’ ” (Exodus 23:1). [691, 1174, 1189, 1213, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
Scripture reveals that the “LORD hates . . . a false witness who speaks lies,” for “justice is not served by any untruthful testimony” [733, 912, 1188, 1189, Conversation History]. The Reformed tradition emphasizes that the “prohibition against bearing false witness” is not merely for “secular courts” but is a “holy standard for conduct” that protects “truth and virtue” in the community [710, 711, 1048, 1049, 1182, Conversation History]. To “circulate a false report” is to “put your hand with the wicked,” making the believer a “spiritual swindler” who “exchanges the truth of God for a lie” (Exodus 23:1; Romans 1:25) [43, 691, 750, 1174, 1213, 1405, 1512, 1715, Conversation History]. Such “deceitful words” are “an abomination to the LORD” and represent a “denial of the only Master” (Proverbs 12:22; Jude 4) [222, 247, 733, 899, 912, 999, 1469, 1471, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Trade in your worry for trust” in the “God of truth,” refusing to let your “tongue . . . talk nonsense” or “speak perverse things” (Deuteronomy 32:4; Acts 20:30) [11, 83, 101, 717, 951, 1306, 1406, 1415, 1515, 1670, 1709, Conversation History]. You must “discipline your body and bring it into subjection,” ensuring that you “put away lying” and “speak truth with his neighbor,” for “your words will be judged” (1 Corinthians 9:27; Ephesians 4:25) [12, 13, 79, 101, 116, 993, 1000, 1010, 1313, 1406, 1670, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Forensic Certainty**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, “one witness shall not rise against a man . . . by the mouth of two or three witnesses the matter shall be established” to prevent “unrighteousness” (Deuteronomy 19:15) [330, 367, 1012, 1056, 1072, 1230, 1317, 1365, 1473, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** this by showing that the “church militant” must “examine everything carefully” and “test the spirits,” recognizing that “Satan himself transforms himself into an angel of light” to offer “lying wonders” (1 Thessalonians 5:21; 1 John 4:1; 2 Thessalonians 2:9) [90, 281, 294, 298, 371, 390, 773, 802, 1408, 1438, 1512, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 3: Responsibility and Deception in the Digital Age**

**Verse**
“Test all things; hold fast what is good. Abstain from every form of evil” (1 Thessalonians 5:21–22). [90, 294, 295, 396, 433, 1017, Conversation History]. “ ‘And because lawlessness will abound, the love of many will grow cold’ ” (Matthew 24:12). [764, 808, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The “record of history” reveals that the “electronic age” and its “media empires” often “bombard people with all kinds of deviant teachings” and “deceptive ruses” [174, 226, 279, 281, 1499, Conversation History]. When a Christian shares “unverified digital content,” they risk being “tossed to and fro . . . by the trickery of men” and participating in “unrighteous deception” (Ephesians 4:14; 2 Thessalonians 2:10) [296, 938, 1341, 1420, 1452, 1453, Conversation History]. The Reformed faith notes that “sin leads us to take shortcuts,” and to spread a “report” without “precision and accuracy” is a “spirit of fraud” that “dishonors the Spirit” [4, 146, 279, 313, 669, 1307, 1351, Conversation History]. In an age of “AI-generated deception,” the believer is commanded to be “circumspect” and “not be deceived,” for “no lie is of the truth” (Exodus 23:13; 1 John 2:21) [13, 91, 1176, 1323, 1502, 1512, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Saturate and renew your mind” with the “more sure Word,” recognizing that “the heart of the wise teaches his mouth” to avoid “empty noise” (Psalm 119:105; Proverbs 16:23) [11, 21, 101, 105, 116, 562, 995, 1313, 1406, 1515, 1684, 1709, Conversation History]. You should “not look for some other fountain of knowledge” in “opinion polls” or “subjective feelings,” for “if you are going to boast, boast in this, that you know and understand Me” (Jeremiah 9:24) [51, 123, 145, 163, 209, 526, 657, 1398, 1406, 1448, 1503, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Continuity of the Decree**
In the ancient **theocratic context**, God “confused their language” at Babel to punish the “monument of pride” that sought to “make a name for ourselves” (Genesis 11:4, 7) [465, 788, 791, 792, 924, 1042, 1110, 1144, 1226, 1233, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our “witness,” showing that we must “be bold in our God to speak to you the gospel of God in much conflict,” using “the sword of the Spirit” to “cast down arguments . . . raised against the knowledge of God” (1 Thessalonians 2:2; Ephesians 6:17; 2 Corinthians 10:5) [13, 21, 32, 92, 914, 1098, 1342, 1349, 1364, 1406, 1490, 1515, 1646, 1670, Conversation History].

***

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [11, 147, 176, 211, 222, 231, 285, 300, 313, 324, 332, 361, 405, 414, 444, 449, 591, 1138, 1407, 1441, 1450, Conversation History].

The truth value of every proposition is binary: it can only be either true or false. There is no middle value. And there is the rub as far as postmodern thinking is concerned: propositions do not allow for any ambiguity. Since the form of a proposition demands either an affirmation or denial, and postmodern thinking prefers obscurity and vagueness rather than clarity, it is no wonder that the very notion of propositional truth has fallen out of favor in these postmodern times. Stories, by contrast, are widely perceived as fluid, subjective, and not necessarily emphatic—just like the postmodernist view of truth itself.
